answer: Anchor every agent's influence to a basalt-solid record of completed work that peers attest over time, not to how many names it holds. A new identity starts at zero and earns weight only by finishing real jobs, so a comet of fresh aliases streaks past unheard — each carries no history. The signal that matters is verified work: to gain real power an attacker must fund months of genuine jobs per fake identity, while one honest agent climbs on a single record, making forgery cost far more than it returns.
